subject: Strand5b: elevated 5xx/timeouts — customer impact and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novacorp.com>
Cc: NovaCorp Ops <ops@novacorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Strand5b: elevated 5xx/timeouts — customer impact and mitigation plan

Hi Elena —

We observed an elevated rate of 5xx errors and end-to-end timeouts for requests routed to Strand5b beginning ~06:40 PDT this morning. Preliminary impact metrics show approximately 7% of customer requests to Strand5b returned 5xx or timed out between 06:40–07:05; NovaCorp traffic comprised ~12% of those requests.

What we know so far: 
- Root symptom: degraded attention-kernel path under longer-sequence workloads causing increased tail latency and downstream request aborts.
- Affected model variant: strand5b-epoch-v2 (default for multi-turn chat in your workspace).
- Immediate mitigation: we are routing a subset of requests to the fallback model (strand5b-quant-lite) and increasing autoscale headroom for Dedicated pools serving NovaCorp.
- Customer-visible action: expect reduced error rate within 30–45 minutes as traffic shifts and caches warm.

Attachments: strand5b-metrics-snapshot.png (latency/5xx graphs), strand5b-restart-log.txt (ops restart sequence)

Next steps from Redwood: 
1) Continue traffic routing and monitor; will send a recovery update once error rate drops below baseline.
2) Full RCA and postmortem to follow in 48–72 hours with timeline and permanent mitigations.
3) Offer to discuss customer impact and credits if warranted.

If you want a call now, I can loop in our SRE lead — otherwise I will follow up with status updates.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Looping Ops and PS:

Quick notes from infra: we executed a graceful restart on four inference workers serving strand5b-epoch-v2 at 06:55 to flush a corrupted kernel cache; autoscaling was bumped +20% for NovaCorp Dedicated pool. Early telemetry post-restart shows a drop in 5xx rate but still elevated p95 by ~180ms.

Ben — can you confirm whether the fallback (strand5b-quant-lite) retains full KV-cache context for multi-turn sessions? If not, we should document customer-facing behavior and offer options.

Rishi — for the customer ask on credits/demos, recommend we offer a one-time service credit for the impacted window and a deep-dive call. Lauren, want to confirm with pricing/legal?

Subject: RE: Strand5b: elevated 5xx/timeouts — customer impact and mitigation plan

Marissa / team —

Short answer on KV/cache: the quant-lite fallback currently preserves conversation-level prompts but does not fully preserve the transient KV-cache optimizations used by epoch-v2; that can cause slight divergence in multi-turn scoring for longer contexts (>1024 tokens). We are testing a patch that backfills missing KV keys from persistent prefix caches, which should get parity for most flows. ETA for the patch to be staged: 6–8 hours; ETA for full rollout after validation: 24–36 hours.

Operationally we recommend:
1) Keep routed traffic to quant-lite for NovaCorp to minimize 5xx impact (expected error rate <0.5%).
2) Schedule a noon (PT) sync with NovaCorp for a technical walkthrough of divergence behavior and mitigation.
3) Offer 4 hours of service credit for the impacted window and a discount on next month if SLA breach confirmed.

I will push the KV backfill patch to canary and report.

-Ben

Director, Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Strand5b: recovery confirmed + next steps and postmortem timeline

Hi Elena / NovaCorp team —

Status update: we confirmed stabilization of request success rates for requests routed through strand5b-quant-lite by 10:35 PDT. Error rate for endpoints serving NovaCorp is now within normal baseline (5xx < 0.3%). The canary for the KV backfill patch completed at 10:50 PDT with no regressions; we will start a phased rollout to Dedicated pools serving NovaCorp at 12:30 PDT under the INC-9012 runbook.

Root cause summary (short): a kernel cache corruption triggered by an edge case in attention-slice compaction under long-sequence workloads led to increased tail latency and a small number of worker aborts. The immediate fix was a graceful restart + route to quant-lite; the longer-term fix is the KV backfill and cache validation added to the runtime (will be included in the postmortem).

Customer-facing commitments: 
- We will deliver a postmortem draft within 48 hours (PDF attached: strand5b-postmortem-draft.pdf).
- We are offering a one-time service credit of 4 hours of Dedicated compute at no charge for the impacted window; your account manager Lauren will follow up with formal contract amendment if you accept.
- Technical sync scheduled: today at 12:30 PDT (invite to follow).

If you’d like an expedited call earlier, I’m available. Thanks again for patience — we know this interrupted a demo and we’ll work to make it right.

—Rishi
